title: POC weekly bench readout - latency / cost concessions (HelionCare)
next_steps: Redwood to run extended 60k qps soak and share raw logs (by 2026-03-06)
Send secure security pack and SOC2 report link (by 2026-03-05)
Provision one dedicated slot for 24h head-to-head test (by 2026-03-08)
Follow-up sync to review soak results and routing policy (calendar invite for 2026-03-10)
action_items: Priya Shah - prepare throughput chart comparing 95th p99 latencies vs baseline (due 2026-03-05)
Jordan Martinez - share pilot pricing appendix and dedicated slot cost breakdown (due 2026-03-04)
Sarah Ng (HelionCare) - provide list of required compliance artifacts and KMS contact (due 2026-03-06)
Marcus Lee - run internal micro-bench with sample traffic generator and send logs (due 2026-03-05)
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-03 | Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jordan M., Priya S., Luis O. / Dr. Emma Kline, Marcus L., Sarah N., Tom R.
summary: Weekly POC readout focused on latency and unit-cost tradeoffs vs HelionCare's incumbent. Redwood presented delta charts showing improved median and p95 in routed requests with KV prefix caching enabled; HelionCare raised concerns about tail spikes under bursty traffic and encryption/KMS integration. Agreement to run a 24h dedicated-slot soak and share security artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec. um quick note, today's goal: share the latest bench numbers and decide next actions on soak and security.
[00:12] Dr. Emma Kline: great, thanks. Marcus and I are on screen, we've got about 40 minutes.
[00:18] Priya Shah: ok jumping in - slide 3 shows the head-to-head baseline. median token latency down ~18% on our routed path, p95 down ~12%. these numbers are with prefix KV cache warmed and batching tuned at 32.
[00:34] Marcus Lee: can you repeat the p95 numbers? I think last week they were closer to baseline.
[00:38] Priya Shah: yeah so the difference is the routing policy - we routed high-probability traffic to the quantized variant with batching 32/continuous batching, other traffic to hosted. that mix gave us the delta - there is a note about the model variant mismatch causing a few JSON structure diffs.
[00:55] Tom Reynolds: JSON diffs were something we flagged - we need deterministic outputs for our downstream parsers. did you run the structural eval?
[01:02] Priya Shah: we ran the eval harness, small regressions on a couple of prompts. SE recommends a soft-rollback on those prompt families and to use the unquantized runtime for them while still using quantized for the bulk.
[01:12] Dr. Emma Kline: ok that could work but costs matter. our CFO will push back on running unquantized at scale. what's the unit cost delta?
[01:20] Jordan Martinez: good call - slide 6 shows unit cost ladder: at our configuration host+quantized routing yields roughly 0.62x the incumbent per-token cost; enabling unquantized for 15% of requests moves us to ~0.85x. still cheaper but we should confirm accuracy tradeoffs.
[01:36] Sarah Ng: on security side we need encryption at rest integration with our KMS, audit logs exported to Splunk, and SSO mapping to roles. do you have SOC2 and ISO attestations?
[01:45] Jordan Martinez: yes - we have SOC2 Type II. I'll send the security packet after the call - includes SOC2, pen test summary, and an architecture note on KMS integrations.
[01:53] Marcus Lee: any network egress issues with VPC peering? we tried a brief run and saw occasional 200ms spikes.
[01:59] Priya Shah: those spikes correspond to cold-KV misses; we saw them mainly during sudden burst patterns. continuous KV cache warmers reduce frequency but don't eliminate tail. Q: are your traffic patterns synthetic spiky or human-chatty?
[02:14] Marcus Lee: both - our production mix has diurnal bursts plus occasional agent-forwarded spikes.
[02:18] Priya Shah: ok we propose a fallback policy: route to dedicated instances during sustained bursts, and a short lived hosted fallback for overflow. that keeps latency SLOs and constrains cost.
[02:29] Dr. Emma Kline: fallback sounds good. what about canarying and automatic rollback if accuracy regresses?
[02:35] Priya Shah: Redwood has a canary rollout built into the control plane - you can pin prompt-sets, run A/B, and auto-fallback to baseline variant if quality drops below threshold. the auto-fallback has a 99.9% trigger option for critical workloads. (transcription note: '99.9' maybe misread as 'nine nine nine')
[02:52] Tom Reynolds: curious about the soak plan - how long and what windows?
[02:55] Jordan Martinez: propose a 24h dedicated-slot soak at peak mix with our traffic generator hitting 60k requests over the period. we'll capture p50/p95/p99, KV miss rates, and token-cost metrics.
[03:05] Marcus Lee: 60k over 24h seems low - can you do a 6h steady at peak QPS and then a 12h diurnal run?
[03:12] Priya Shah: yes we can rearrange - we'll do a 6h high-QPS window plus 18h variable. important to see both tails and sustained throughput.
[03:20] Dr. Emma Kline: what exactly do you need from our side to schedule the dedicated slot?
[03:24] Jordan Martinez: approval for the slot and an email agreement to run the soak, plus an IP allowlist for the load generator and a brief KMS test token.
[03:31] Sarah Ng: we'll need an SOC2 addendum and the KMS contact - I'll put those in an email.
[03:35] Luis Ortega: I'll capture that and follow up with a secure link to the SOC2 docs.
[03:39] Priya Shah: one more technical note - when KV cache misses align with bursty decoder lengths we saw p99 spikes up to ~420ms; under steady state it's closer to 220ms. baseline vendor had 480-550ms p99 in our tests.
[03:55] Marcus Lee: so worst-case you're better but there are spikes. can we tune batching further? what about reducing max tokens?
[04:02] Priya Shah: yes batching smaller for short prompts helps reduce tail; we can also route short prompts to a smaller sequence-optimized kernel variant. reduces both latency and cost.
[04:12] Dr. Emma Kline: can Redwood guarantee fallback to incumbent if there's a regression at 3am? our ops team wants auto-failover to incumbent vendor for safety.
[04:20] Jordan Martinez: we can put in a policy that fails over to your incumbent as an emergency fallback — requires a lightweight connector but doable. we usually recommend Redwood-hosted fallback for faster recovery but we'll support whichever you prefer.
[04:30] Tom Reynolds: connector effort estimate?
[04:33] Priya Shah: engineering estimate about 3-5 days for the connector integration and testing.
[04:37] Dr. Emma Kline: ok put that in the next steps.
[04:40] Jordan Martinez: quick commercial note - if you take a 3-month dedicated pilot we can offer a commit discount on dedicated slots; I will include that in the pricing appendix.
[04:48] Marcus Lee: good. can you also share the raw latency CSVs? our SREs will ingest them into Grafana.
[04:52] Priya Shah: yes - we'll upload to the secure drive link: https://redwood.example/drive/helioncare-poc-030326 (note: placeholder link).
[04:59] Sarah Ng: last question on data retention - logs stored from the soak, how long do you keep them?
[05:03] Jordan Martinez: default is 30 days, can be extended for enterprise accounts; we can also set retention per-tenant.
[05:09] Dr. Emma Kline: that should be fine for now.
[05:12] Priya Shah: recap then: 1) we run 24h soak (6h peak + 18h diurnal) on dedicated slot; 2) send SOC2 and KMS doc pack; 3) perf team to upload raw CSVs and p95/p99 charts; 4) pricing appendix with dedicated slot discounts.
[05:27] Jordan Martinez: thanks all - we'll aim to kick off the soak Friday EOD pending your OK. I'll follow up by email with the calendar invite.
[05:35] Dr. Emma Kline: thanks, looking forward.
[05:38] Marcus Lee: thanks everyone.
[05:40] Jordan Martinez: meeting adjourned.
